coupling.rationale: Pages depend on narrow PokeApi methods and pure helpers, and the client/server boundary is an exemplary seam; the tangles (LoadState→NotFound import, card list→service injection, the server's mirrored route table) are mild and findable.

abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions that carry real variation (cards, badges, sorting, API client, format helpers) stretch to similar cases cleanly; the one copy-paste seam is the ~25 lines of per-page resource/title/load-state wiring that each detail page repeats, so a new Items section copies a page's scaffolding rather than reusing it.

findings.issue: A shared/ component imports pages/not-found, inverting the layering: shared code depends on page code.
findings.suggestion: Move the Not-found markup into shared/ (or inline it in LoadState); pages should depend on shared, never the reverse.

findings.issue: Home builds its own CardData array separately from PokeApi.cardsFor, duplicating card-assembly logic; a change to card shape or sprite derivation touches both sites.
findings.suggestion: Have cardsFor accept species refs (or extract a shared card builder) so Home reuses the same path as move/ability/type pages.

findings.issue: DETAIL_ROUTES duplicates the app's route and resource knowledge; every added/removed detail page needs an edit here.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for the 404-probing goal, but document the pairing next to app.routes.ts or derive both from one shared list.

findings.issue: Presentational card list injects the PokeApi data service solely to build sprite URLs, coupling rendering to the data layer.
findings.suggestion: Accept a sprite URL (or URL resolver) as an input, keeping the component data-source-agnostic.

findings.issue: Fabricates NamedResource objects with url: '' to satisfy typeLabels' signature — a type-driven hack.
findings.suggestion: Change typeLabels to accept a list of type names; the url field is unused there.

findings.issue: Loading/error markup hand-rolled here and in types-page.ts:14-16 instead of reusing shared/load-state.ts, giving three slightly different loading states.
findings.suggestion: Extend LoadState (e.g. an error-message input) and use it on every page.

findings.issue: The default API origin literal appears in api-config.ts, server/server.mjs:27 and README — three places to update if the default changes.
findings.suggestion: Fine as config duplication, but a comment cross-referencing the other two spots would help.

findings.issue: Resource methods and models accumulate per feature; removing a section (e.g. abilities) leaves ability()/Ability as unflagged dead code.
findings.suggestion: When removing a feature, grep for the resource name; consider co-locating per-feature API slices with their pages.

summary: This is an easy codebase to own: one self-contained component per route, a single cached API client behind an injection token, tested pure helpers for the tricky logic, and shared card/badge/table abstractions that stretch across all four list pages. The costs are small and enumerable: card assembly is duplicated for the home page, loading-state markup is re-written per page instead of consolidated, a shared component imports from pages, and the Node server mirrors the route table. All five edit scenarios land in one to three predictable files.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Route + page file delete cleanly and the nav has no link, but the Pokémon page's spec-mandated Abilities section, its data mapping, the server DETAIL_ROUTES entry, and now-dead PokeApi.ability/Ability model all need edits or deliberate dead-code cleanup.

scenarios.change: Fix the card sprite for species whose default Pokémon has a different name (e.g. Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: Sprite URL derivation is centralized in PokeApi.spriteUrl with a single rendering consumer (PokemonCardList), and cardsFor maps every move/ability/type list to CardData; only Home assembles cards separately, so most fixes touch one or two core files and automatically cover every list.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: All lists render through one shared component, so sorting there covers move/ability/type pages in a single edit; making it consistent with home's dex-ordered pagination requires also touching the home-data/home ordering.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: PokeApi's byName pattern, format helpers, LoadState, syncPageTitle, PokemonCardList and TypeBadge are all reusable unchanged; but each detail page hand-wires its own resource/loader/title scaffolding, so the new item page copies ~90 lines of structure from move-page.ts, plus a route line and a server DETAIL_ROUTES entry.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: Consumers see only the API_BASE_URL token; the origin is injected via a meta tag written by the server at request time, and caching is one Map plus one TTL constant in PokeApi.get — a rule change is a single-file edit with no ripple.
